If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in late horizon (days 25–30) to avoid overestimation.  
If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–10) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (≥0.67 then ≤0.33 or vice versa) within last 5 days, apply a 2% correction to mid-horizon (days 11–20) toward the sentiment’s recent direction.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast shows persistent upward trend, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast shows persistent downward trend, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% in early horizon to avoid underestimation.  
If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) and forecast is flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast by 1.0–1.5% in mid-horizon to align with sentiment’s diminishing momentum.
